profile.content:
# Landscape operational profile

Source authority: WORLD_RENDERING_SPEC §§1–5, ASSET_PRODUCTION_SPEC general/world/transparency rules, LANDSCAPE_GENERATION_CONTRACT_V1, and the selected Phase 8 prompt-manifest sections. Use this focused profile for ordinary image commands; read full source specs for changes to these rules.

- One crisp pixel-art PNG per generation call. Attach the exact immutable registry reference as pixels; a written path is insufficient. For a revision also attach the current accepted/working layer and preserve its composition except for the requested change. Approved direction updates in the selected prompt take precedence over older reference content.
- Preserve location, landmark relationships, lighting, palette and pixel-art language. No characters, hazards, HUD, text, checkerboard or baked shared clouds. Approved scene-specific exceptions, such as SA01's decorative snake, remain in its stage lock.
- New source canvas: 2172×724, 8-bit non-interlaced PNG. MID/GROUND require RGBA and real transparency; FAR is fully opaque. Exact registry dimensions/types override generic prompt dimensions for a preserved approved exception: NA03 GROUND is 2170×725. Never normalize it for convenience.
- Runtime viewport 960×540; running surface 410; landscape source width 2172; FAR/MID/GROUND offsets all zero; scale multipliers FAR 1.25, MID 1, GROUND 1. Actual draw scale is `960/2172 × multiplier`. MID anchor 621 and GROUND anchor 393 map to 410. Zero offsets do not mean drawing MID/GROUND's canvas top at Y=0.
- FAR owns opaque skyline/foundation and useful scenery behind MID transparency. MID owns middle-distance silhouettes, intentional sky openings and enough lower authored coverage to overlap GROUND. GROUND owns a continuous level surface at source Y=393 and solid terrain depth to the bottom, with appropriate transparent space above. No synthetic backing or offset changes to hide missing art.
- Inspect the actual stage configuration before blaming an image: registry activation, inner renderer, outer bootstrap, saved authoring draft and reset must agree. Active stages use the shared contract; pending stages keep their legacy baseline until their full set is integrated. Legacy sprite normalization is unrelated to landscape source width and must not be globally replaced.
- Full PNG integrity/dimensions/alpha checks plus isolated, repeat and composite review are required. Check MID lower coverage/transition and GROUND surface/depth visually; a fully opaque FAR can hide a bad MID in an aggregate alpha statistic. Edge-delta numbers alone cannot prove a seamless repeat. Inspect in the actual app at scroll offsets and in Inspector previews before asking for acceptance.
- Approved horizontal-edge-only deterministic repair may correct a repeat seam without moving landmarks/anchors, rescaling, changing dimensions/alpha ownership or hiding a structural defect. Other artwork edits use image generation unless explicitly authorized. The historic NA03 overscan treatment is asset-specific, not blanket permission to stretch future artwork.
- Correct only the requested layer or proven configuration defect. Never change sibling assets, gameplay, character/hazard calibration or approved image bytes as an optimization. Stop after checks and visual inspection pass; final acceptance belongs to the user on the deployed integrated stage.

sharedRules.hazardProfile:
# New-stage hazard profile

Applies to new AF/AS/OC/AN files. Source: HAZARD_SPEC and REMAINING_CONTINENTS_PLAN. Existing accepted atlases/calibrations stay unchanged.

- Ground atlas: 2172×724 RGBA; two 1086×724 cells, GROUND1 left / GROUND2 right. Source contact (543,620); at least 32px clear cell gutters. No scenery/labels.
- Flying atlas: 2172×724 RGBA; four 543×724 cells. Fixed source body anchor (271,362), right-facing source, stable anatomy, four distinct wing poses and continuous loop. Every flock member animates.
- Record source-facing and intended gameplay-facing separately. Directional hazards approaching from the right face left in gameplay; retain pixels and use the matching `flipX` transform. Nondirectional objects use neither automatic mirroring nor an invented facing.
- Supply source regions, crops/frame crops, anchors, frame order/FPS and usable starting scale/body bounds. Crops retain anchors. Starting bounds represent solid bodies, excluding decorative wings/tails/leaves. Inspect basic rendering and credible size with the character reference at 960×540/mobile; do not inflate a small species for visibility.
- Ground uses Y=410 and the explicit source anchor; flying uses the shared HIGH/LOW starting placement. These are provisional metadata, not accepted character-relative calibration. No global physics, clearance or speed changes to rescue art.
- Validate source integrity/alpha, gutters, ground contact pixels, distinct frame bytes and animation/pose stability. Inspect composition and basic rendering. Structural checks alone do not prove animation quality or collision fairness.
- End asset production with the versioned asset-ready handoff and exact five-file hashes. The editor-next Workbench agent imports it; the user calibrates and saves. Iterative grounding, flight height, hitbox fairness, Jump/Slide windows, difficulty and spawn-spacing balancing belong there. Repeated zero-hit courses are not an asset handoff gate.
- Later playable release retains real contact, collision, finish and gameplay validation. Never mark unperformed checks passed. Keep genuine renderer/scheduler bug fixes and regression tests.
- A GROUND1/GROUND2 revision preserves its sibling's RGBA pixels and metadata exactly. Recover original bytes from Git; never silently regenerate an accepted sibling.
sharedRules.pixelArt: Match the established crisp pixel-art language; no photorealism, painterly blur, vector-flat redesign, smooth 3D, labels, UI or unrelated assets.

profile.content:
# Landscape operational profile

Source authority: WORLD_RENDERING_SPEC §§1–5, ASSET_PRODUCTION_SPEC general/world/transparency rules, LANDSCAPE_GENERATION_CONTRACT_V1, and the selected Phase 8 prompt-manifest sections. Use this focused profile for ordinary image commands; read full source specs for changes to these rules.

- One crisp pixel-art PNG per generation call. Attach the exact immutable registry reference as pixels; a written path is insufficient. For a revision also attach the current accepted/working layer and preserve its composition except for the requested change. Approved direction updates in the selected prompt take precedence over older reference content.
- Preserve location, landmark relationships, lighting, palette and pixel-art language. No characters, hazards, HUD, text, checkerboard or baked shared clouds. Approved scene-specific exceptions, such as SA01's decorative snake, remain in its stage lock.
- New source canvas: 2172×724, 8-bit non-interlaced PNG. MID/GROUND require RGBA and real transparency; FAR is fully opaque. Exact registry dimensions/types override generic prompt dimensions for a preserved approved exception: NA03 GROUND is 2170×725. Never normalize it for convenience.
- Runtime viewport 960×540; running surface 410; landscape source width 2172; FAR/MID/GROUND offsets all zero; scale multipliers FAR 1.25, MID 1, GROUND 1. Actual draw scale is `960/2172 × multiplier`. MID anchor 621 and GROUND anchor 393 map to 410. Zero offsets do not mean drawing MID/GROUND's canvas top at Y=0.
- FAR owns opaque skyline/foundation and useful scenery behind MID transparency. MID owns middle-distance silhouettes, intentional sky openings and enough lower authored coverage to overlap GROUND. GROUND owns a continuous level surface at source Y=393 and solid terrain depth to the bottom, with appropriate transparent space above. No synthetic backing or offset changes to hide missing art.
- Inspect the actual stage configuration before blaming an image: registry activation, inner renderer, outer bootstrap, saved authoring draft and reset must agree. Active stages use the shared contract; pending stages keep their legacy baseline until their full set is integrated. Legacy sprite normalization is unrelated to landscape source width and must not be globally replaced.
- Full PNG integrity/dimensions/alpha checks plus isolated, repeat and composite review are required. Check MID lower coverage/transition and GROUND surface/depth visually; a fully opaque FAR can hide a bad MID in an aggregate alpha statistic. Edge-delta numbers alone cannot prove a seamless repeat. Inspect in the actual app at scroll offsets and in Inspector previews before asking for acceptance.
- Approved horizontal-edge-only deterministic repair may correct a repeat seam without moving landmarks/anchors, rescaling, changing dimensions/alpha ownership or hiding a structural defect. Other artwork edits use image generation unless explicitly authorized. The historic NA03 overscan treatment is asset-specific, not blanket permission to stretch future artwork.
- Correct only the requested layer or proven configuration defect. Never change sibling assets, gameplay, character/hazard calibration or approved image bytes as an optimization. Stop after checks and visual inspection pass; final acceptance belongs to the user on the deployed integrated stage.

sharedRules.hazardProfile:
# New-stage hazard profile

Applies to new AF/AS/OC/AN files. Source: HAZARD_SPEC and REMAINING_CONTINENTS_PLAN. Existing accepted atlases/calibrations stay unchanged.

- Ground atlas: 2172×724 RGBA; two 1086×724 cells, GROUND1 left / GROUND2 right. Source contact (543,620); at least 32px clear cell gutters. No scenery/labels.
- Flying atlas: 2172×724 RGBA; four 543×724 cells. Fixed source body anchor (271,362), right-facing source, stable anatomy, four distinct wing poses and continuous loop. Every flock member animates.
- Record source-facing and intended gameplay-facing separately. Directional hazards approaching from the right face left in gameplay; retain pixels and use the matching `flipX` transform. Nondirectional objects use neither automatic mirroring nor an invented facing.
- Supply source regions, crops/frame crops, anchors, frame order/FPS and usable starting scale/body bounds. Crops retain anchors. Starting bounds represent solid bodies, excluding decorative wings/tails/leaves. Inspect basic rendering and credible size with the character reference at 960×540/mobile; do not inflate a small species for visibility.
- Ground uses Y=410 and the explicit source anchor; flying uses the shared HIGH/LOW starting placement. These are provisional metadata, not accepted character-relative calibration. No global physics, clearance or speed changes to rescue art.
- Validate source integrity/alpha, gutters, ground contact pixels, distinct frame bytes and animation/pose stability. Inspect composition and basic rendering. Structural checks alone do not prove animation quality or collision fairness.
- End asset production with the versioned asset-ready handoff and exact five-file hashes. The editor-next Workbench agent imports it; the user calibrates and saves. Iterative grounding, flight height, hitbox fairness, Jump/Slide windows, difficulty and spawn-spacing balancing belong there. Repeated zero-hit courses are not an asset handoff gate.
- Later playable release retains real contact, collision, finish and gameplay validation. Never mark unperformed checks passed. Keep genuine renderer/scheduler bug fixes and regression tests.
- A GROUND1/GROUND2 revision preserves its sibling's RGBA pixels and metadata exactly. Recover original bytes from Git; never silently regenerate an accepted sibling.
sharedRules.pixelArt: Match the established crisp pixel-art language; no photorealism, painterly blur, vector-flat redesign, smooth 3D, labels, UI or unrelated assets.

artDirection.authority: User direction, 2026-09-19; see the composition, identity and scale section of the plan.
artDirection.scope: Remaining-continent proposals; existing approved artwork is not reopened.
artDirection.FAR: One recognizable local landmark or dominant natural formation, readable in the runtime composite behind MID and away from repeat joins.
artDirection.MID: One restrained, unique local sign of life: settlement/frontage, everyday-use detail or static background wildlife. No people or gameplay hazards baked into scenery.
artDirection.originality: Compare identities and visible silhouettes against existing and proposed campaign elements. No reused species/objects, renamed duplicates or recolors as new hazards; shared background materials are not signature elements.
artDirection.scale: Judge visible subjects at 960x540 and normal mobile presentation relative to characters, architecture and depth. Reject subjects that read too small or need implausible enlargement. Preserve canonical transforms and physics.
artDirection.selectionReviewStatus: Africa agent selections resolved; remaining nine proposals still need campaign comparison. Visual size/reference inspection remains stage-specific.
artDirection.approval: Requirements and workflow direction approved. Unresolved selection changes remain review items; generated artwork still requires deployed-stage acceptance.
